claim.quote: The measured value of the neutron EDM is $d_{\rm n} = (0.0\pm1.1_{\rm stat}\pm0.2_{\rm sys})\times10^{-26}e\,{\rm cm}$.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date; the journal version is Phys. Rev. Lett. 124, 081803 (2020). The abstract reports the measured value; the upper limit quoted in the paper body is not recorded here.

name: Measurement of the permanent electric dipole moment of the neutron

significance.value: Consistent with zero: (0.0 ± 1.1 stat ± 0.2 sys) x 10^-26 e cm

summary.plain: The nEDM experiment at the Paul Scherrer Institute measured the neutron’s electric dipole moment and found it consistent with zero: (0.0 ± 1.1 stat ± 0.2 sys) in units of 10^-26 electron charge times centimetre. No dipole moment is seen.
summary.technical: Ramsey separated-oscillating-field measurement with ultracold neutrons at PSI using an Hg-199 co-magnetometer and an array of optically pumped Cs magnetometers, blinded analysis by two groups: d_n = (0.0 ± 1.1 stat ± 0.2 sys) x 10^-26 e cm from 54068 cycles taken in 2015-2016.

title: Measurement of the permanent electric dipole moment of the neutron
why_it_matters: The abstract places the result in the long history of EDM experiments probing physics that violates time-reversal invariance.
